1	# Plan: prompt
2	
3	**Status:** drafting
4	**Authors:** claude-code, codex
5	**Created:** 2026-05-08
6	
7	## TLDR
8	
9	Ship `entire investigate` as a hidden top-level command surfaced through
10	`entire labs`. It runs a non-TUI marvin-style round-robin loop across
11	launchable, hook-enabled agents (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli), bootstraps
12	a findings doc + timeline (including prior Entire context when there is no
13	seed doc), and tags each spawned session with a new `agent_investigate` Kind
14	so the next commit condenses the investigation into `entire/checkpoints/v1`
15	alongside `entire review` runs. GitHub issue/PR URLs seed the loop through
16	`gh`; a local manifest plus an `entire investigate fix` helper lets users feed
17	accepted findings into a follow-up coding session. Biggest tradeoff:
18	investigate gets its own `HasInvestigation` umbrella flag and
19	`Kind.IsInvestigate()` predicate rather than reusing review's umbrella, so the
20	feature stays semantically honest at the cost of updating every local reader
21	that currently only knows about review.
22	
23	## Problem / Motivation
24	
25	`marvin investigate` (POC at `/Users/alisha/Projects/marvin`) runs a
26	multi-agent investigation against a seeded question or doc and produces a
27	findings + timeline artifact. We want to graduate that workflow into the
28	Entire CLI as a real, supported command — `entire investigate` — that reuses
29	the `entire review` scaffolding so investigations are saved, linked to
30	checkpoints, and condensed onto `entire/checkpoints/v1` the same way reviews
31	are. Today nothing in `entire` captures pre-implementation investigation
32	work; ad-hoc agent runs lose their context on the next commit, and there is
33	no provenance trail tying "we investigated X" to the commit it informed.
34	
35	Investigations also need to be triggerable from external work tracking. The
36	user should be able to point the command at a GitHub issue or PR (or any
37	code-issue link) and have it pull the linked content as the seed, without
38	hand-copying the issue body into a doc.
39	
40	## Goals
41	
42	- Add a new `entire investigate` command that mirrors `entire review`'s
43	  placement: top-level command, listed under `entire labs` as experimental,
44	  invoked directly (no `entire labs investigate` namespace).
45	- Reuse `entire review` scaffolding for persistence and provenance: an
46	  `ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*` env-var handshake parallel to `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*`,
47	  lifecycle adoption to tag the session, an `attach` subcommand,
48	  condensation onto `entire/checkpoints/v1` via the existing multi-session
49	  checkpoint format, and a new `HasInvestigation` umbrella flag on
50	  `CheckpointSummary`.
51	- Match the `marvin investigate` UX where it makes sense: accept either a
52	  `--topic` (matching marvin's `--question`) or a `[seed-doc]` positional
53	  path, port marvin's investigate prompt body verbatim, drive a round-robin
54	  loop with stances and quorum, and persist a findings doc + timeline.
55	- Add a `--issue-link <url>` flag that accepts GitHub issue and PR URLs
56	  (resolved via `gh issue|pr view --json`), turns the issue body into a
57	  seed findings doc, and falls back with a clear "save to a file and pass
58	  as a positional `[seed-doc]`" error for unsupported hosts.
59	- Provide a way to feed a saved investigation back into a follow-up agent
60	  run: `entire investigate fix [<run-id>]` mirrors `entire review --fix` —
61	  resolves the manifest, composes a prompt that says "use these findings
62	  as context, do not re-investigate", and launches a regular coding agent
63	  session.
64	- Persist the findings as part of checkpoint metadata and local manifests so
65	  `entire status`, `entire checkpoint explain --json`, and
66	  `entire investigate --findings` / `fix` can surface them. Dedicated
67	  `entire search` investigation UX is out of scope for this PR because it
68	  depends on the cloud search service, not only this CLI repo.
69	
70	## Non-Goals
71	
72	- No TUI. Explicitly out of scope (user: "don't do tui"). Marvin's
73	  `investigate_tui.go` overview model is not being ported. Output is a
74	  printed turn-N banner + per-turn log file, with `--verbose` to tee
75	  stdout to the terminal.
76	- Not a wholesale port of marvin: only the investigate flow is in scope,
77	  not `marvin plan`, `marvin work`, `marvin wt`, `marvin clean`, or
78	  `marvin memory`. Marvin's `--brainstorm` editor flow is also out of
79	  scope for this PR — investigate launches straight into the loop.
80	- Not changing how `entire review` works, its settings schema, its storage
81	  format, or its checkpoint metadata layout. Investigate sits alongside
82	  review on the same scaffolding; review behavior is unchanged.
83	- Not introducing a new checkpoint storage primitive or branch.
84	  Investigations live in the existing `entire/checkpoints/v1` metadata
85	  with a new `Kind`, not a separate branch or store.
86	- Not building a generic web-fetch / scraping framework. `--issue-link`
87	  resolves GitHub issues and PRs through the `gh` CLI; non-GitHub URLs
88	  fail with a clear error directing the user to seed-doc instead.
89	- Not moving `entire review` under a `labs` namespace or otherwise
90	  changing its invocation path — `entire labs` remains a discovery
91	  command per the prior decision (#1130).
92	- Not extending `Kind.IsReview()` to cover investigate. Investigate gets
93	  its own `Kind.IsInvestigate()` predicate and its own `HasInvestigation`
94	  umbrella; the existing review umbrella keeps its narrow meaning.
95	- Not changing the remote `entire search` service or inventing a new
96	  search-side investigation badge/filter in this PR. Search may still match
97	  investigation content through whatever the existing backend indexes, but
98	  this plan does not depend on or promise new search-service behavior.
99	
100	## Proposal
101	
102	### 1. Command surface
103	
104	```
105	entire investigate                              # Run with config (or first-run picker)
106	entire investigate [seed-doc]                   # Use seed file as starting findings
107	entire investigate --topic "<question>"         # Or pass a topic directly
108	entire investigate --issue-link <github-url>    # Pull GH issue/PR body as seed
109	entire investigate --agents <csv>               # Override configured agents
110	entire investigate --max-turns N                # Per-agent turn budget (default: 3)
111	entire investigate --quorum N                   # Approvals required (default: all)
112	entire investigate --output <path>              # Override findings doc location
113	entire investigate --continue <run-id>          # Resume a paused/stalled run
114	entire investigate --edit                       # Re-open the config picker
115	entire investigate --findings                   # Browse local investigation manifests
116	entire investigate --verbose                    # Tee per-turn stdout to terminal
117	
118	entire investigate fix [<run-id>]               # Open a coding agent with findings as context
119	entire investigate attach <session-id>          # Tag an existing session as investigate (post-hoc)
120	```
121	
122	Cobra placement: `investigate.NewCommand(buildInvestigateDeps(newInvestigateAttachCmd()))`
123	in `cmd/entire/cli/root.go`, parallel to how `cliReview.NewCommand(...)` is
124	wired today for `entire review`. The command is `Hidden: true` (mirrors
125	review during the labs phase), and an `experimentalCommands` entry is added
126	in `cmd/entire/cli/labs.go` so `entire labs` lists it.
127	
128	Validation rules:
129	- At most one of `[seed-doc]`, `--topic`, `--issue-link` may be set per run.
130	- `--continue` is mutually exclusive with the seed/topic/issue inputs.
131	- Every selected agent must satisfy both constraints review already depends on:
132	  a non-interactive launcher/spawner exists, and Entire hooks are installed for
133	  that agent in the current repo. Config or `--agents` overrides that name an
134	  agent without hooks fail with the same style of actionable error as
135	  `entire review` ("run `entire configure --agent <name>` first").
136	- `fix` and `attach` are sibling subcommands of `investigate`, registered the
137	  same way `review attach` is wired today via `Deps.AttachCmd`.
138	
139	### 2. Settings schema
140	
141	Add an `Investigate` field to `EntireSettings` in
142	`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`:
143	
144	```json
145	{
146	  "investigate": {
147	    "agents": ["claude-code", "codex"],
148	    "max_turns": 3,
149	    "quorum": 0,
150	    "always_prompt": "Be skeptical and cite line numbers."
151	  }
152	}
153	```
154	
155	Differs from `Review` by design: review configures *per-agent skill lists*
156	because each agent runs different skills; investigate runs the same shared
157	investigate prompt across all agents, so per-agent customization adds no
158	value and `agents` is a flat list. `quorum: 0` means "all agents must
159	approve" (matches marvin). `always_prompt` is appended to every turn's
160	prompt, parallel to `ReviewConfig.Prompt`.
161	
162	First-run setup: `runInvestigateConfigPicker` shows a multi-select of agents
163	that satisfy two predicates in the current repo: (1) a `Spawner` is
164	registered for the agent (today: claude-code, codex, gemini-cli — the same
165	three agents that already have `buildReviewCmd` helpers and reviewer.go
166	files), AND (2) `agent.Get(name).AreHooksInstalled(ctx)` returns true.
167	Non-spawnable agents (cursor, opencode, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli) and
168	test-only agents (vogon) are filtered out at predicate (1). Agents without
169	hooks are excluded at predicate (2) because investigate's value proposition
170	is automatic session tagging via `UserPromptSubmit` plus later condensation,
171	not a best-effort transcript scrape.
172	
173	### 3. Storage layout
174	
175	Findings doc + timeline (in worktree, optionally committed by the user):
176	
177	```
178	.entire/investigations/<slug>.md            # Findings doc
179	.entire/investigations/<slug>-timeline.md   # Per-turn timeline with stances
180	```
181	
182	Per-run state and transcripts (under git common dir, never committed,
183	per-worktree-safe by living next to `.git/entire-sessions/`):
184	
185	```
186	.git/entire-investigations/state/<run-id>.json          # Round, turn count, stances
187	.git/entire-investigations/transcripts/<run-id>/
188	  turn-1-claude-code.log
189	  turn-2-codex.log
190	  ...
191	.git/entire-investigations/manifests/<timestamp>-<run-id>.json   # For --findings browsing
192	```
193	
194	`<slug>` is `slugifyTopic(topic)` (port the helper from
195	`marvin/internal/cli/plan.go`). `<run-id>` is a 12-hex random ID generated at
196	loop start and embedded in env vars so all per-turn agent sessions can be
197	correlated.
198	
199	Bootstrap behavior should mirror marvin's setup path rather than inventing a
200	new document contract. If the user passed `[seed-doc]`, copy it verbatim into
201	the findings doc and derive the topic from `# Investigation: ...`, then the
202	first markdown H1, then the filename as a last resort. If no seed doc was
203	passed, render a scaffold with the same sections marvin uses today (`TLDR`,
204	`Question`, `Prior work`, `System under investigation`, `Approach`,
205	`Findings`, `Unknowns / Assumptions`, `Conclusion`) and pre-fill a
206	`## Prior Entire Context` block by running the current Entire-history lookup
207	flow (`entire search "<topic>" --json --limit 3 --repo "*"` plus short
208	checkpoint explain excerpts for returned hits). `--issue-link` should
209	generate a scaffold-compatible seed doc instead of a one-off markdown shape so
210	the first agent turn starts from the same document structure as every other
211	investigation run.
212	
213	Per-session state and condensation reuse the existing pipeline unchanged:
214	
215	- `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json` stores `Kind = "agent_investigate"`,
216	  `InvestigatePrompt`, plus three new fields: `InvestigateRunID`,
217	  `InvestigateRound`, `InvestigateTurn`, `InvestigateAgent`.
218	- On the next user commit, the existing PostCommit condense path copies the
219	  session into `entire/checkpoints/v1` with `Kind` and `ReviewSkills`-style
220	  metadata fields propagated. Multi-session checkpoint format already supports
221	  multiple sessions per checkpoint; each turn's session lands in its own
222	  numbered subfolder (`0/`, `1/`, ...).
223	
224	### 4. Env-var handshake
225	
226	Parallel package `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/env.go`:
227	
228	```go
229	const (
230	    EnvSession      = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_SESSION"      // "1"
231	    EnvAgent        = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_AGENT"        // "claude-code"
232	    EnvRunID        = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_RUN_ID"       // 12-hex
233	    EnvRound        = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_ROUND"        // "1", "2", ...
234	    EnvTurn         = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_TURN"         // overall turn index
235	    EnvTopic        = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_TOPIC"        // human-readable topic
236	    EnvPrompt       = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_PROMPT"       // composed prompt
237	    EnvFindingsDoc  = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_FINDINGS_DOC" // absolute path
238	    EnvTimelineDoc  = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_TIMELINE_DOC" // absolute path
239	    EnvStartingSHA  = "ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_STARTING_SHA" // anti-stale-env guard
240	)
241	```
242	
243	`AppendInvestigateEnv` mirrors `review.AppendReviewEnv`: strips any existing
244	`ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*` entries from `base`, then appends the contract
245	variables. Each spawned process inherits its own copy, so concurrent
246	worktrees and concurrent investigations cannot leak env into each other.
247	
248	### 5. Loop architecture
249	
250	Port marvin's `runPlanLoop` into `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/loop.go`,
251	specialised to the investigate mode:
252	
253	```go
254	func runInvestigateLoop(ctx context.Context, deps LoopDeps) (Result, error)
255	```
256	
257	Per-turn flow:
258	1. Hash findings doc + timeline before the turn and again after the turn, and
259	   persist `PlanChanged` / `TimelineChanged`-style booleans in run state and
260	   manifests for operator visibility. Mirror marvin's current bookkeeping here
261	   instead of inventing extra control flow around "no edit" turns.
262	2. Resolve the agent's spawner via `deps.SpawnerFor(agentName)` — this is
263	   the new shared interface (see §6) that returns an `*exec.Cmd` builder.
264	3. Compose the per-turn prompt via `ComposeInvestigatePrompt(in)` (port of
265	   marvin's `buildInvestigatePrompt`, including the shared prior-decisions /
266	   prior-claims / prior-fixes / memory-tools preamble plus the
267	   investigate-specific body, with `Files: { Findings, Timeline }` pointing
268	   at the worktree paths).
269	4. Spawn the agent with `cmd.Stdout = MultiWriter(perTurnLogFile, optionalTeeStdout)`.
270	5. After exit, parse the timeline file for the new `## Turn N — <agent>`
271	   entry, read the `**Stance:**` line, and record it in run state. If the
272	   header or stance line is missing/unparseable, record `unknown` and warn,
273	   matching marvin's current parser behavior rather than synthesizing a fake
274	   `request-changes` vote.
275	6. Persist run state to `.git/entire-investigations/state/<run-id>.json` after
276	   every turn so `--continue` can resume.
277	
278	Loop termination:
279	- Quorum reached when the count of `approve` stances in the most recent
280	  fully-played round is ≥ `quorum` (default `len(agents)`).
281	- `paused` when ctx is cancelled (Ctrl+C) or an agent fails twice in a row.
282	- `stalled` when `max-turns * len(agents)` turns have been played without
283	  quorum.
284	
285	The loop is single-threaded by design — each turn waits for the previous
286	agent to exit before starting the next. This is the correct shape for
287	investigate: agents must read each other's edits to make progress, so
288	parallelism would hurt.
289	
290	### 6. Shared agent spawner
291	
292	Refactor opportunity: `cmd/entire/cli/review/types/template.go` already
293	encapsulates "build *exec.Cmd from RunConfig" via
294	`ReviewerTemplate.BuildCmd`. Extract a smaller `Spawner` interface to
295	`cmd/entire/cli/agent/spawn/` so both review and investigate consume it:
296	
297	```go
298	type Spawner interface {
299	    Name() string
300	    // BuildCmd returns a non-started exec.Cmd. The caller passes the
301	    // composed env (already including ENTIRE_REVIEW_* or ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*
302	    // produced by review.AppendReviewEnv / investigate.AppendInvestigateEnv)
303	    // and the composed prompt. Spawner stays env-contract-agnostic.
304	    BuildCmd(ctx context.Context, env []string, prompt string) *exec.Cmd
305	}
306	```
307	
308	Per-agent implementations live in each agent's package
309	(`agent/claudecode/spawner.go`, `agent/codex/spawner.go`,
310	`agent/geminicli/spawner.go`) and are tiny — the existing `buildReviewCmd`
311	bodies (argv shape + stdin wiring) move here, with `AppendReviewEnv`
312	factored out to the caller. Review wraps a `Spawner` inside its existing
313	parser-driven `ReviewerTemplate` (BuildCmd now reads `cfg.Prompt =
314	ComposeReviewPrompt(cfg)` then `env := AppendReviewEnv(os.Environ(),
315	agentName, cfg, prompt); spawner.BuildCmd(ctx, env, prompt)`); investigate
316	wraps the same `Spawner` with a log-file-piping driver and
317	`AppendInvestigateEnv` instead. Review's existing argv contract tests
318	(`agent/<name>/reviewer_test.go`) move to the spawner package and are
319	re-pointed at the new helper, preserving the regression net.
320	
321	Do not reuse `agent.LauncherFor` for this path. The existing `LaunchCmd`
322	implementations in `agent/claudecode/claude.go`, `agent/codex/codex.go`, and
323	`agent/geminicli/gemini.go` are foreground TTY-oriented entrypoints
324	(`claude <prompt>`, `codex <prompt>`, `gemini <prompt>`) intended for normal
325	interactive coding sessions and `review --fix`, not for a headless loop that
326	must inject `ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*`, capture deterministic stdout, and return
327	without user keystrokes. Investigate needs the review-style non-interactive
328	builders, not the interactive launcher contract.
329	
330	This is a small refactor (≈ 60 LOC moved across three files) and is
331	included in this PR because investigate cannot ship without a way to
332	exec each agent non-interactively, and duplicating the argv constructors
333	would create the kind of drift the env-var contract is designed to prevent.
334	
335	### 7. Lifecycle adoption
336	
337	Add `adoptInvestigateEnv(ctx, state, expectedAgent)` next to
338	`adoptReviewEnv` in `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go`. Same shape: short-circuit
339	if state.Kind already set; check `EnvSession == "1"`; verify `EnvAgent` and
340	`EnvStartingSHA` match; tag state.
341	
342	```go
343	state.Kind = session.KindAgentInvestigate
344	state.InvestigateRunID = os.Getenv(investigate.EnvRunID)
345	state.InvestigateRound = atoiOrZero(os.Getenv(investigate.EnvRound))
346	state.InvestigateTurn = atoiOrZero(os.Getenv(investigate.EnvTurn))
347	state.InvestigateTopic = os.Getenv(investigate.EnvTopic)
348	state.InvestigatePrompt = os.Getenv(investigate.EnvPrompt)
349	```
350	
351	Adoption fires from the same `InitializeSession` site that calls
352	`adoptReviewEnv` today, immediately after. `Kind` is single-valued, so a
353	session is either a review OR an investigate, never both.
354	
355	### 8. Checkpoint metadata changes
356	
357	`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go`:
358	- New const `KindAgentInvestigate Kind = "agent_investigate"`.
359	- New method `Kind.IsInvestigate() bool { return k == KindAgentInvestigate }`.
360	- New `State` fields: `InvestigateRunID`, `InvestigateRound`, `InvestigateTurn`,
361	  `InvestigateTopic`, `InvestigatePrompt` (all `omitempty`).
362	
363	`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`:
364	- New `CommittedMetadata` fields parallel to `ReviewSkills` / `ReviewPrompt`:
365	  `InvestigateRunID`, `InvestigateRound`, `InvestigateTurn`,
366	  `InvestigateTopic`, `InvestigatePrompt`.
367	- New `CheckpointSummary` field: `HasInvestigation bool` with `omitempty`.
368	- Caller-side flag (matching `HasReview`): a new field
369	  `WriteCommittedOptions.HasInvestigation` that the PostCommit dispatcher
370	  computes via `state.Kind.IsInvestigate()` and propagates into the summary
371	  the same way `HasReview` flows today.
372	
373	`committed.go`'s `WriteCommitted` propagates `HasInvestigation` with the
374	existing OR-style merge that protects `HasReview`: if a prior session in
375	this checkpoint already set the flag, keep it set.
376	
377	Local readers must be updated explicitly; they do not "just work" today:
378	
379	- `cmd/entire/cli/status.go` currently only consults `headHasReviewCheckpoint`.
380	  Replace that single-purpose helper with a generic HEAD checkpoint summary
381	  lookup (or parallel helpers backed by one lookup) so status can print
382	  `Review` and `Investigation` lines independently when HEAD's checkpoint
383	  summary carries either umbrella flag.
384	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go` currently exposes `has_review` at the
385	  top level and only review-specific session fields in its JSON envelope.
386	  Add `has_investigation` plus session-level
387	  `investigate_run_id`, `investigate_round`, `investigate_turn`, and
388	  `investigate_topic` fields so `entire checkpoint explain --json` can show
389	  the new metadata without requiring transcript reads.
390	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go` can keep `InvestigatePrompt` out of the
391	  JSON envelope, matching the current review export shape: prompt bodies are
392	  available through transcript/prompt files when explicitly requested, but the
393	  metadata export stays compact.
394	
395	Backwards compat: `omitempty` JSON tag means old metadata is read with
396	zero values; old CLIs reading new metadata see `Kind = "agent_investigate"`
397	as an unknown string and treat the session as "normal" — no review
398	behaviour fires, which is the correct fallback.
399	
400	`entire search` is intentionally not changed here. Its CLI surface talks to a
401	remote search service with its own schema and ranking behavior; this PR only
402	guarantees the local checkpoint metadata and manifests are present for future
403	indexing, not that the cloud service grows an investigation-aware badge or
404	filter in lockstep.
405	
406	### 9. `--issue-link` semantics
407	
408	Implementation in `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/issuelink.go`:
409	
410	```go
411	func ResolveIssueLink(ctx context.Context, url string) (seedDoc []byte, topic string, err error)
412	```
413	
414	1. Parse URL. If host is `github.com` and path matches
415	   `/<owner>/<repo>/(issues|pull)/<n>`, dispatch to `gh issue view` or
416	   `gh pr view` with `--json title,body,author,createdAt,labels,comments`.
417	   Compose a markdown seed doc:
418	
419	   ```
420	   # Investigation: <title>
421	
422	   **Source:** <url>
423	   **Author:** @<author>
424	   **Created:** <createdAt>
425	   **Labels:** <labels>
426	
427	   ## Question
428	
429	   <body>
430	
431	   ## Comments
432	
433	   - **@<commenter> (<createdAt>):** <comment-body>
434	   ...
435	   ```
436	
437	2. If host is `github.com` but path doesn't match, return a clear error
438	   pointing the user at `--topic` or seeding from a file.
439	3. If host is anything else, return:
440	   `"--issue-link only supports GitHub issues and PRs in this release;
441	    save the issue body to a file and pass it as a positional [seed-doc]"`.
442	4. If `gh` is not on PATH, return a clear error: `"--issue-link requires
443	    the gh CLI; install it (https://cli.github.com) or pass [seed-doc]"`.
444	
445	The `gh` invocation is wrapped in a `runGhFn` package var so unit tests can
446	inject a fake. No HTTP client, no scraping, no auth handling — `gh` already
447	owns auth and is the standard Entire users have.
448	
449	Topic derivation: prefer the issue/PR title; fall back to the URL itself if
450	empty. The composed seed doc is written to `<findings-doc-path>` and the
451	loop runs against it.
452	
453	### 10. `entire investigate fix` semantics
454	
455	Mirrors `entire review --fix`. Resolves a manifest by `<run-id>` (or prompts
456	to pick the most recent). Composes a follow-up prompt like:
457	
458	> A prior multi-agent investigation produced these findings. Use them as
459	> grounded context to plan the next step. Do not re-investigate the same
460	> question — assume the findings are correct unless you find direct
461	> evidence to the contrary.
462	>
463	> ## Investigation findings
464	>
465	> <body of `.entire/investigations/<slug>.md`>
466	>
467	> ## Investigation timeline
468	>
469	> <body of `.entire/investigations/<slug>-timeline.md`>
470	
471	Then launches a normal `entire`-aware coding agent session via the existing
472	`launchReviewFixAgent` helper, which is renamed `launchFixAgent` and moved
473	from `cmd/entire/cli/review/fix.go` to a new `cmd/entire/cli/agentlaunch/`
474	package so both review-fix and investigate-fix can call it. The helper's
475	env-stripping step is broadened from `withoutReviewEnv` to also strip
476	`ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*` entries before exec, so a fix session never inherits
477	either set of provenance env vars from its parent. The launched session is
478	a plain coding session, not tagged as review or investigate.
479	
480	This is "the way to feed a saved investigation back into a follow-up agent
481	run for context" called for in the goals.
482	
483	### 11. Picker / first-run setup
484	
485	`runInvestigateConfigPicker` in `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/picker.go`:
486

665	## Alternatives Considered
666	
667	**1. Run agents in parallel (not round-robin).** Rejected. Agents must read
668	each other's findings to converge; parallel runs would either produce
669	non-overlapping findings (no convergence) or require a merge step that
670	re-introduces sequential editing. Marvin chose round-robin for the same
671	reason.
672	
673	**2. Store findings in `~/.entire/investigations/` like marvin does in
674	`~/.marvin/`.** Rejected. Entire is per-repo and ties context to
675	checkpoints; a per-repo path under `.entire/` (worktree) and
676	`.git/entire-investigations/` (state) keeps everything addressable from the
677	repo and survives the same way checkpoints do. Marvin's global home was
678	appropriate for a multi-repo POC; entire's model is repo-scoped.
679	
680	**3. Reuse `Kind = "agent_review"` and extend `IsReview()` to cover
681	investigate, with a new sub-discriminator.** Rejected. Review and
682	investigate produce different artifacts (skills output vs findings doc),
683	have different commit-time UX (re-run guard wording, status banner), and
684	the existing `HasReview` docstring explicitly says it's the umbrella for
685	"any review happened". Conflating the two breaks the umbrella's meaning
686	and forces every downstream reader to disambiguate. A parallel
687	`HasInvestigation` flag is simpler.
688	
689	**4. Build a generic web fetcher behind `--issue-link`.** Rejected per
690	non-goals. `gh` already handles GitHub auth, rate limits, and JSON output;
691	non-GitHub hosts (Linear, GitLab, Jira) need different auth models and
692	response shapes that do not generalise. A pluggable fetcher framework is
693	real engineering and not something we can afford to ship correctly inside
694	this PR. Users with non-GitHub sources can pre-paste content into a seed
695	file in two seconds.
696	
697	**5. Live overview TUI like marvin's `investigate_tui.go`.** Rejected per
698	the user's explicit "don't do tui". The non-TUI design also unblocks
699	running investigate inside another agent session (e.g. a Claude Code
700	session calling `entire investigate` via Bash) — TUI sinks block on
701	keypresses that never arrive in that context. Per-turn log files are
702	greppable, archivable, and visible without ANSI gymnastics.
703	
704	**6. Skip the spawner refactor; duplicate argv builders for investigate.**
705	Rejected. Three agents × two callers (review + investigate) = six places
706	where argv must stay aligned. The next agent-flag tweak (e.g. a future
707	`--permission-mode` change) would silently drift across callers. Sharing
708	through a small `Spawner` interface costs ≈ 60 LOC and prevents the drift.
709	
710	## Risks & Mitigations
711	
712	- **Risk: `gh` not installed.** Detected at `--issue-link` resolution time;
713	  surface a clear error pointing at the `gh` install URL and the seed-doc
714	  fallback. Not blocking for the rest of the command.
715	- **Risk: agent fails to modify the findings doc.** The pre-turn hash check
716	  still detects "no edit", but the loop should surface that as bookkeeping
717	  (`PlanChanged=false` / `TimelineChanged=false`) plus an `unknown` stance
718	  warning when the timeline entry is missing, rather than inventing a vote the
719	  agent never cast. This keeps the control flow aligned with marvin's current
720	  behavior while still making silent turns obvious in logs and manifests.
721	- **Risk: stale `ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_*` env from a parent shell tagging the
722	  wrong session.** Same protection as review: `EnvAgent` must match the
723	  hook's agent and `EnvStartingSHA` must match the session's base commit.
724	  Both must hold for adoption to fire; either mismatch leaves the session
725	  untagged with a logged warning.
726	- **Risk: the shared spawner refactor regresses review argv.** Contract
727	  tests in `agent/<name>/spawner_test.go` pin the exact argv string per
728	  agent; review's existing argv tests (e.g. `claudecode/reviewer_test.go`)
729	  also serve as a regression net via the wrapper.
730	- **Risk: investigation findings doc lands in the user's commit
731	  unintentionally.** Entire does not guarantee `.entire/` is ignored in every
732	  repo, and this repo's tracked `.gitignore` does not ignore it today. The
733	  findings doc is still a deliberate deliverable, so we do not auto-add a
734	  gitignore entry or auto-stage it; we surface the file path on completion so
735	  users can choose whether to commit it or ignore `.entire/investigations/`
736	  explicitly in their own repo.
737	- **Risk: `entire investigate` invoked from inside an existing agent
738	  session (Claude Code calling Bash → entire investigate).** Works by
739	  design — no TUI, env per process — but the inner sessions inherit
740	  `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` if the outer was a review. The
741	  `withoutReviewEnv`-style strip in `AppendInvestigateEnv` removes any
742	  `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` entries before appending investigate vars to prevent
743	  cross-tagging.
744	- **Risk: product plan overpromises cloud search behavior that this repo
745	  cannot ship.** Mitigation: scope the PR to local checkpoint/manifests UX
746	  only (`status`, `checkpoint explain`, `--findings`, `fix`) and document
747	  that dedicated `entire search` investigation surfacing depends on the
748	  remote service, so it is not part of this change set.

750	## Decision
751	
752	Approved direction: ship as a single PR titled `feat(investigate): add
753	entire investigate command (labs)`. Includes the cobra command, the loop
754	driver, the env-var contract, the lifecycle adoption, the

756	shared spawner refactor, the `--issue-link` resolver, the `fix` and

761	- Env-var contract correctness (multi-tenant inheritance, stale-env

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents. The quality of its work will be significantly higher if run on a platform with subagent support (such as Claude Code or Codex). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Read plan file
2. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
3. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
4. If no concerns: Create TodoWrite and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - Ensures isolated workspace (creates one or verifies existing)
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot
digraph when_to_use {
    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot

    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];

        "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];
        "Code quality reviewer subagent approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Implementer subagent fixes quality issues" [shape=box];
        "Mark task complete in TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    }

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" [shape=box];
    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";

    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];
    "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="re-review"];
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent (./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md)" [label="yes"];

```

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```

[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - Ensures isolated workspace (creates one or verifies existing)
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

1	// Package review contains the env-var contract between `entire review` (which
2	// spawns the agent process) and the lifecycle hook (which adopts the session).
3	// These names are stable API; renaming any constant is a breaking change.
4	//
5	// Design rationale: each spawned agent inherits its own copy of the process
6	// environment, so multi-tenant correctness (multiple worktrees, multi-agent
7	// runs) holds by construction — one agent's env vars cannot bleed into
8	// another agent's session. The lifecycle UserPromptSubmit hook reads these
9	// env vars to tag the in-flight session as a review session (Kind =
10	// "agent_review") and records which skills were run.
11	package review
12	
13	import (
14		"encoding/json"
15		"fmt"
16		"strings"
17	
18		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
19	)
20	
21	const (
22		// EnvSession is the review-session indicator. `entire review` sets this
23		// to "1" on the spawned agent process; the lifecycle hook treats any
24		// other value (including unset) as a normal coding session. Kept as a
25		// sentinel string rather than a bool so future versions can carry
26		// additional metadata in the value without breaking the contract.
27		EnvSession = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_SESSION"
28	
29		// EnvAgent is the name of the agent spawned for the review (e.g.
30		// "claude-code"). The lifecycle hook requires this to match the hook's
31		// agent before tagging the session, preventing stale exported review env
32		// from tagging sessions for a different agent.
33		EnvAgent = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_AGENT"
34	
35		// EnvSkills is a JSON-encoded []string of skill invocations passed to the
36		// agent verbatim (e.g. `["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr","/test-auditor"]`).
37		// Use EncodeSkills / DecodeSkills to round-trip the value safely.
38		EnvSkills = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_SKILLS"
39	
40		// EnvPrompt is the full prompt text sent to the agent at review start. The
41		// lifecycle hook stores this so the checkpoint records what the agent was
42		// asked to review.
43		EnvPrompt = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_PROMPT"
44	
45		// EnvStartingSHA is the git commit SHA that was HEAD when `entire review`
46		// was invoked. The lifecycle hook requires this to match the session's
47		// initial base_commit before tagging the session, so stale env from an old
48		// HEAD does not mark a later normal session as a review.
49		EnvStartingSHA = "ENTIRE_REVIEW_STARTING_SHA"
50	)
51	
52	// EncodeSkills serialises a slice of skill invocation strings to a JSON value
53	// suitable for storing in the ENTIRE_REVIEW_SKILLS environment variable.
54	// An empty or nil slice encodes to the literal string "[]".
55	func EncodeSkills(skills []string) (string, error) {
56		if len(skills) == 0 {
57			return "[]", nil
58		}
59		b, err := json.Marshal(skills)
60		if err != nil {
61			return "", fmt.Errorf("encode skills: %w", err)
62		}
63		return string(b), nil
64	}
65	
66	// DecodeSkills deserialises a value previously produced by EncodeSkills.
67	// An empty string decodes to a nil slice (no skills configured).
68	// Any other value that is not valid JSON returns an error.
69	func DecodeSkills(encoded string) ([]string, error) {
70		if encoded == "" {
71			return nil, nil
72		}
73		var skills []string
74		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(encoded), &skills); err != nil {
75			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode skills: %w", err)
76		}
77		return skills, nil
78	}
79	
80	// AppendReviewEnv adds the ENTIRE_REVIEW_* env vars to base, returning
81	// the new slice. Used by per-agent reviewers in their AgentReviewer.Start
82	// implementations to propagate the review-session contract to spawned
83	// agent processes.
84	//
85	// agentName must be the agent's stable registry key (e.g. "claude-code").
86	// cfg carries skills and the starting SHA. prompt is the full composed
87	// prompt text (result of ComposeReviewPrompt).
88	//
89	// Any pre-existing ENTIRE_REVIEW_* entries in base are stripped before the
90	// new values are appended. This handles nested invocations (an `entire
91	// review` run spawning another agent that calls `entire review`) and stale
92	// inheritance from a parent shell — the most-recent values must win, with
93	// no chance of duplicate keys whose precedence is implementation-defined.
94	func AppendReviewEnv(base []string, agentName string, cfg reviewtypes.RunConfig, prompt string) []string {
95		skillsJSON, _ := EncodeSkills(cfg.Skills) //nolint:errcheck // EncodeSkills only fails on json.Marshal([]string), which is infallible
96		out := make([]string, 0, len(base)+5)
97		for _, kv := range base {
98			if isReviewEnvEntry(kv) {
99				continue
100			}
101			out = append(out, kv)
102		}
103		return append(out,
104			EnvSession+"=1",
105			EnvAgent+"="+agentName,
106			EnvSkills+"="+skillsJSON,
107			EnvPrompt+"="+prompt,
108			EnvStartingSHA+"="+cfg.StartingSHA,
109		)
110	}
111	
112	func withoutReviewEnv(base []string) []string {
113		out := make([]string, 0, len(base))
114		for _, kv := range base {
115			if isReviewEnvEntry(kv) {
116				continue
117			}
118			out = append(out, kv)
119		}
120		return out
121	}
122	
123	// isReviewEnvEntry reports whether kv is a "KEY=VALUE" entry whose key is
124	// one of the ENTIRE_REVIEW_* contract variables.
125	func isReviewEnvEntry(kv string) bool {
126		for _, prefix := range []string{
127			EnvSession + "=",
128			EnvAgent + "=",
129			EnvSkills + "=",
130			EnvPrompt + "=",
131			EnvStartingSHA + "=",
132		} {
133			if strings.HasPrefix(kv, prefix) {
134				return true
135			}
136		}
137		return false
138	}

202	
203		// 2. Load config. A load error means the settings file exists but is
204		// malformed (Load returns a default-filled object when the file is
205		// missing). Surface the error instead of silently opening the picker,
206		// which would cause SaveReviewConfig to write over the user's other
207		// settings with an empty EntireSettings{}.
208		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
209		if err != nil {
210			cmd.SilenceUsage = true
211			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Failed to load settings: %v\n", err)
212			fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Fix `.entire/settings.json` and re-run `entire review`.")
213			return silentErr(err)
214		}
215		if s == nil || len(s.Review) == 0 {
216			if !ConfirmFirstRunSetup(ctx, out) {
217				return nil
218			}
219			picked, pickErr := RunReviewConfigPicker(ctx, out, deps.GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled)
220			if pickErr != nil {
221				return pickErr
222			}
223			if s == nil {
224				s = &settings.EntireSettings{}
225			}
226			s.Review = picked
227			fmt.Fprintln(out)
228			fmt.Fprintln(out, "Setup complete — running review now.")
229		}
230	
231		// 3. Resolve installed agents and determine the dispatch path.
232		//
233		// Three paths:
234		//   - Multi-agent: 2+ launchable eligible agents AND no --agent override →
235		//     show multi-select picker then RunMulti. Steps 3.5, 3.6, and the
236		//     single-agent skill-verify guard are skipped; each reviewer pulls
237		//     its own skills from settings at spawn time via RunConfig.
238		//   - Single-agent (default): 1 or fewer launchable eligible agents, OR
239		//     --agent override set. Falls through to the full agent-selection and
240		//     validation path below (steps 3–3.6).
241		installed := deps.GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled(ctx)
242		if agentOverride == "" {
243			launchableEligible := computeLaunchableEligible(s, installed, deps.ReviewerFor)
244			if len(launchableEligible) >= 2 {
245				return runMultiAgentPath(ctx, cmd, launchableEligible, s, innerDeps, deps, out)
246			}
247		}
248	
249		// Single-agent path: pick agent, verify hooks + skills, scope, run.
250	
251		// 3a. Base selection on the eligible set (configured AND installed):
252		//   - 0 eligible: fall through; SelectReviewAgent below errors with the
253		//     full configured map (clearer "no installed agent" diagnostic than
254		//     a silent fail).
255		//   - 1 eligible: use it directly. This matters when the alphabetically-
256		//     first configured agent isn't installed but exactly one other is —
257		//     without this, SelectReviewAgent would default to the alphabetical
258		//     first and the verify-hooks check below would error needlessly.
259		//   - 2+ eligible: prompt with single-select (non-launchable agents reach
260		//     this branch since computeLaunchableEligible filtered them out above).
261		if agentOverride == "" {
262			eligible := ComputeEligibleConfigured(s, installed)
263			switch {
264			case len(eligible) == 1:
265				agentOverride = eligible[0].Name
266			case len(eligible) > 1:
267				fn := innerDeps.promptForAgentFn
268				if fn == nil {
269					fn = PromptForAgent
270				}
271				picked, pickErr := fn(ctx, eligible)
272				if pickErr != nil {
273					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
274					fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), pickErr.Error())
275					return silentErr(pickErr)
276				}
277				if picked == "" {
278					// Defensive: empty picker return must not fall through to
279					// alphabetical-first default.
280					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
281					emptyErr := errors.New("agent picker returned empty agent name")
282					fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), emptyErr.Error())
283					return silentErr(emptyErr)
284				}
285				agentOverride = picked
286			}
287		}
288	
289		agentName, cfg, err := SelectReviewAgent(s.Review, agentOverride)
290		if err != nil {
291			cmd.SilenceUsage = true
292			fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), err.Error())
293			return silentErr(err)
294		}
295	
296		return runSingleAgentPath(ctx, cmd, agentName, cfg, installed, deps, out)
297	}

299	// runSingleAgentPath completes a single-agent review: verifies hooks + skills,
300	// guards against re-review, resolves scope, then dispatches via Run or
301	// RunMarkerFallback.
302	func runSingleAgentPath(
303		ctx context.Context,
304		cmd *cobra.Command,
305		agentName string,
306		cfg settings.ReviewConfig,
307		installed []types.AgentName,
308		deps Deps,
309		out io.Writer,
310	) error {
311		silentErr := deps.NewSilentError
312	
313		// 3.5. Verify hooks are installed for the selected agent.
314		found := false
315		for _, n := range installed {
316			if string(n) == agentName {
317				found = true
318				break
319			}
320		}
321		if !found {
322			cmd.SilenceUsage = true
323			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
324				"Hooks are not installed for %q. Run `entire configure --agent %s` first, "+
325					"or remove %q from review settings.\n",
326				agentName, agentName, agentName)
327			return silentErr(fmt.Errorf("hooks not installed for %s", agentName))
328		}
329	
330		// 3.6. Verify configured skills are actually installed on disk.
331		ag, agErr := agent.Get(types.AgentName(agentName))
332		if agErr != nil {
333			return fmt.Errorf("resolve agent %s: %w", agentName, agErr)
334		}
335		if err := VerifyConfiguredSkillsInstalled(ctx, ag, cfg); err != nil {
336			cmd.SilenceUsage = true
337			fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), err.Error())
338			return silentErr(err)
339		}
340	
341		// 4. Re-run guard: check if HEAD's checkpoint already has a review.
342		if reviewed, meta := deps.HeadHasReviewCheckpoint(ctx); reviewed {
343			var proceed bool
344			form := newAccessibleForm(huh.NewGroup(
345				huh.NewConfirm().
346					Title(fmt.Sprintf("Already reviewed: %s. Proceed anyway?", meta)).
347					Value(&proceed),
348			))
349			if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
350				fmt.Fprintln(out, "prompt cancelled")
351				return err //nolint:wrapcheck // propagate huh cancellation
352			}
353			if !proceed {
354				fmt.Fprintln(out, "Review cancelled.")
355				return nil
356			}
357		}
358	
359		// 5. Resolve HEAD SHA and worktree root.
360		worktreeRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
361		if err != nil {
362			return fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root: %w", err)
363		}
364	
365		// 6. Resolve HEAD SHA and detect scope.
366		headSHA, shaErr := currentHeadSHA(ctx, worktreeRoot)
367		if shaErr != nil {
368			return fmt.Errorf("resolve HEAD: %w", shaErr)
369		}
370		scopeBaseRef := detectScope(ctx, worktreeRoot, out)
371		checkpointContext := ""
372		if deps.ReviewCheckpointContext != nil {
373			checkpointContext = deps.ReviewCheckpointContext(ctx, worktreeRoot, scopeBaseRef)
374		}
375	
376		runCfg := reviewtypes.RunConfig{
377			ScopeBaseRef:      scopeBaseRef,
378			CheckpointContext: checkpointContext,
379			StartingSHA:       headSHA,
380		}
381		applyReviewConfig(&runCfg, cfg)
382	
383		// 7. Branch on launchability.
384		reviewer := deps.ReviewerFor(agentName)
385		if reviewer == nil {
386			// Non-launchable: write marker (with scope-aware prompt) and print guidance.
387			return RunMarkerFallback(ctx, agentName, runCfg, worktreeRoot, out)
388		}
389	
390		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(ctx)
391		defer cancelRun()
392	
393		canPrompt := interactive.CanPromptInteractively()
394		sinks := composeSingleAgentSinks(singleAgentSinkInputs{
395			out:       out,
396			isTTY:     interactive.IsTerminalWriter(out) && canPrompt,
397			canPrompt: canPrompt,
398			agentName: agentName,
399			cancelRun: cancelRun,
400		})
401		if tuiSink, ok := findTUISink(sinks); ok {
402			tuiSink.Start()
403			defer tuiSink.Wait()
404		}
405	
406		summary, waitErr := Run(runCtx, reviewer, runCfg, sinks)
407		writePostReviewManifest(ctx, out, worktreeRoot, headSHA, summary, "")
408		if waitErr != nil && runCtx.Err() == nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
409			// Non-cancellation error: surface to caller.
410			return fmt.Errorf("review run: %w", waitErr)
411		}
412		return nil
413	}
414	
415	// detectScope computes the scope base ref for the current repo and prints a
416	// scope banner to out on success. Best-effort: on any failure, returns an
417	// empty string and prints no banner so the run proceeds in degraded mode.
418	func detectScope(ctx context.Context, worktreeRoot string, out io.Writer) (scopeBaseRef string) {
419		if repo, openErr := git.PlainOpen(worktreeRoot); openErr == nil {
420			if stats, statsErr := ComputeScopeStats(ctx, repo); statsErr == nil {
421				fmt.Fprintln(out, formatScopeBanner(stats))
422				return stats.BaseRef
423			} else { //nolint:revive // else-after-return is clearer here for the error-path log
424				logging.Debug(ctx, "review scope detection failed", slog.String("error", statsErr.Error()))
425			}
426		} else {
427			logging.Debug(ctx, "review repo open failed", slog.String("error", openErr.Error()))
428		}
429		return ""
430	}
431	
432	// runMultiAgentPath handles the multi-agent review flow: shows the multi-select
433	// picker, collects an optional per-run prompt, builds per-agent RunConfigs,
434	// then runs all selected agents concurrently via RunMulti.
435	//
436	// This path skips the single-agent validation steps (3.5 hooks, 3.6 skills,
437	// re-run guard) for brevity — computeLaunchableEligible has already ensured
438	// each eligible agent has hooks installed and a Reviewer available.
439	func runMultiAgentPath(
440		ctx context.Context,
441		cmd *cobra.Command,
442		launchableEligible []AgentChoice,
443		s *settings.EntireSettings,
444		innerDeps runReviewDeps,
445		deps Deps,
446		out io.Writer,
447	) error {
448		// Note: skill verification is intentionally skipped here. The
449		// computeLaunchableEligible filter in the dispatch fork already
450		// guarantees every agent in launchableEligible has hooks installed
451		// AND a non-nil ReviewerFor mapping, so a per-agent verify pass would
452		// be redundant.
453		silentErr := deps.NewSilentError
454	
455		// Show multi-select picker (or use injected stub in tests).
456		pickerFn := innerDeps.multiPickerFn
457		if pickerFn == nil {
458			pickerFn = PickAgents
459		}
460		picked, pickErr := pickerFn(ctx, launchableEligible)
461		if pickErr != nil {
462			return handlePickerError(cmd, silentErr, pickErr)
463		}
464	
465		// Resolve worktree root and HEAD SHA for scope detection.
466		worktreeRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
467		if err != nil {
468			return fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root: %w", err)
469		}
470		headSHA, shaErr := currentHeadSHA(ctx, worktreeRoot)
471		if shaErr != nil {
472			return fmt.Errorf("resolve HEAD: %w", shaErr)
473		}
474	
475		scopeBaseRef := detectScope(ctx, worktreeRoot, out)
476		checkpointContext := ""
477		if deps.ReviewCheckpointContext != nil {
478			checkpointContext = deps.ReviewCheckpointContext(ctx, worktreeRoot, scopeBaseRef)
479		}
480	
481		// Build per-agent reviewers with individual RunConfigs (each agent has
482		// its own skills + always-prompt from s.Review[name]).
483		reviewers := make([]reviewtypes.AgentReviewer, 0, len(picked.Names))
484		for _, name := range picked.Names {
485			agentCfg := s.Review[name] // zero value is safe (empty skills/prompt)
486			reviewer := deps.ReviewerFor(name)
487			if reviewer == nil {
488				// Shouldn't happen given launchableEligible was filtered for
489				// ReviewerFor != nil, but be defensive.
490				cmd.SilenceUsage = true
491				return silentErr(fmt.Errorf("agent %q is not launchable but appeared in eligible list", name))
492			}
493			// Wrap the reviewer so it sees the per-agent RunConfig at Start time.
494			// We cannot pass a different RunConfig per reviewer in RunMulti's
495			// current API (all reviewers share one RunConfig). Instead, build a
496			// configuredReviewer adapter that injects per-agent skills into
497			// RunConfig before forwarding to the underlying reviewer.
498			reviewers = append(reviewers, &perAgentConfiguredReviewer{
499				inner: reviewer,
500				cfg: runConfigWithReviewConfig(reviewtypes.RunConfig{
501					PerRunPrompt:      picked.PerRun,
502					ScopeBaseRef:      scopeBaseRef,
503					CheckpointContext: checkpointContext,
504					StartingSHA:       headSHA,
505				}, agentCfg),
506			})
507		}
508	
509		// Compose sinks based on TTY detection.
510		// TTY mode: [TUISink, DumpSink] — TUI owns the live dashboard; DumpSink
511		// renders the post-run narrative after TUI dismisses (RunFinished is called
512		// on each sink in order, and TUISink.RunFinished blocks until user dismisses).
513		// Non-TTY mode: [DumpSink] alone.
514		//
515		// A derived context is used so the TUI's Ctrl+C handler can cancel the run
516		// via the same cancelRun function that the orchestrator's context is built on.
517		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(ctx)
518		defer cancelRun()
519	
520		agentNames := make([]string, len(reviewers))
521		for i, r := range reviewers {
522			agentNames[i] = r.Name()
523		}
524		aggregateOutput := ""
525	
526		// TUI requires both:
527		//   - terminal stdout (otherwise ANSI codes corrupt redirected output)
528		//   - a promptable stdin (otherwise the post-run dismissal loop blocks
529		//     forever — happens when entire review is invoked from inside an
530		//     agent like Claude Code or Gemini CLI, where stdout is a TTY but
531		//     keypresses are never delivered)
532		sinks := composeMultiAgentSinks(multiAgentSinkInputs{
533			out:               out,
534			isTTY:             interactive.IsTerminalWriter(out) && interactive.CanPromptInteractively(),
535			canPrompt:         interactive.CanPromptInteractively(),
536			agentNames:        agentNames,
537			cancelRun:         cancelRun,
538			runContext:        runCtx,
539			synthesisProvider: deps.SynthesisProvider,
540			promptYN:          deps.PromptYN,
541			perRunPrompt:      picked.PerRun,
542			onSynthesisResult: func(result string) {
543				aggregateOutput = result
544			},
545		})
546		if tuiSink, ok := findTUISink(sinks); ok {
547			tuiSink.Start()
548			defer tuiSink.Wait()
549		}
550	
551		summary, waitErr := RunMulti(runCtx, reviewers, reviewtypes.RunConfig{}, sinks)
552		writePostReviewManifest(ctx, out, worktreeRoot, headSHA, summary, aggregateOutput)
553		if waitErr != nil && runCtx.Err() == nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
554			return fmt.Errorf("review run: %w", waitErr)
555		}
556		return nil
557	}
558	
559	// handlePickerError maps multi-picker error sentinels to the appropriate
560	// command-layer response.
561	//   - ErrPickerCancelled → return nil (user cancelled; no error shown)
562	//   - ErrNoAgentsSelected → surface error to user
563	//   - other errors → surface to user
564	func handlePickerError(cmd *cobra.Command, silentErr func(error) error, pickErr error) error {
565		if errors.Is(pickErr, ErrPickerCancelled) {
566			return nil
567		}
568		cmd.SilenceUsage = true
569		fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), pickErr.Error())
570		return silentErr(pickErr)
571	}
572	
573	// multiAgentSinkInputs collects the parameters composeMultiAgentSinks needs.
574	// It exists so tests can drive the helper with explicit isTTY / canPrompt
575	// values instead of monkey-patching interactive helpers at run time.
576	//
577	// isTTY here means "the TUI sink is safe to compose" — production callers
578	// AND IsTerminalWriter(out) with CanPromptInteractively() before passing
579	// it in, since the TUI both writes ANSI to stdout AND reads keypresses
580	// from stdin. A terminal-stdout-but-non-interactive-stdin scenario (an
581	// agent host like Claude Code invoking `entire review`) must NOT use the
582	// TUI — its dismissal loop would block forever.
583	type multiAgentSinkInputs struct {
584		out               io.Writer
585		isTTY             bool
586		canPrompt         bool
587		agentNames        []string
588		cancelRun         context.CancelFunc
589		runContext        context.Context
590		synthesisProvider SynthesisProvider
591		promptYN          func(ctx context.Context, question string, def bool) (bool, error)
592		perRunPrompt      string
593		onSynthesisResult func(result string)
594	}
595	
596	type singleAgentSinkInputs struct {
597		out       io.Writer
598		isTTY     bool
599		canPrompt bool
600		agentName string
601		cancelRun context.CancelFunc
602	}
603	
604	// composeMultiAgentSinks builds the sink slice for a multi-agent run.
605	//
606	//   - Non-TTY: [DumpSink] alone — narrative dump only, no live UI, no prompts.
607	//   - TTY: [TUISink, DumpSink, SynthesisSink?] — TUI owns the live dashboard;
608	//     DumpSink renders the post-run narrative; SynthesisSink (if a provider is
609	//     configured AND stdin can prompt) appends the y/N synthesis offer.
610	//
611	// The synthesis sink is only appended when canPrompt is true: without a
612	// promptable stdin, the y/N form would never resolve. SynthesisSink also
613	// guards on InputTTY internally (defense in depth) but suppressing it here
614	// avoids constructing a sink that will silently no-op.
615	func composeMultiAgentSinks(in multiAgentSinkInputs) []reviewtypes.Sink {
616		if !in.isTTY {
617			return []reviewtypes.Sink{DumpSink{W: in.out}}
618		}
619		sinks := []reviewtypes.Sink{
620			NewTUISink(in.agentNames, in.cancelRun, in.out),
621			DumpSink{W: in.out},
622		}
623		if in.synthesisProvider != nil && in.canPrompt {
624			sinks = append(sinks, SynthesisSink{
625				Provider:     in.synthesisProvider,
626				Writer:       in.out,
627				InputTTY:     in.canPrompt,
628				PromptYN:     in.promptYN,
629				PerRunPrompt: in.perRunPrompt,
630				RunContext:   in.runContext,
631				OnResult:     in.onSynthesisResult,
632			})
633		}
634		return sinks
635	}
636	
637	func writePostReviewManifest(
638		ctx context.Context,
639		out io.Writer,
640		worktreeRoot string,
641		headSHA string,
642		summary reviewtypes.RunSummary,
643		aggregateOutput string,
644	) {
645		if summary.Cancelled || len(summary.AgentRuns) == 0 {
646			return
647		}
648		manifest, err := localReviewManifestFromCurrentState(ctx, worktreeRoot, headSHA, summary, aggregateOutput)
649		if err != nil {
650			logging.Debug(ctx, "review manifest not written", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
651			warnManifestNotWritten(out, "could not load session state: "+err.Error())
652			return
653		}
654		if len(manifest.Sources) == 0 {
655			logging.Debug(ctx, "review manifest not written: no matching review sessions")
656			warnManifestNotWritten(out, "review session was not tagged as a review (env-var handshake did not reach the hook)")
657			return
658		}
659		if err := writeLocalReviewManifest(ctx, manifest); err != nil {
660			logging.Debug(ctx, "review manifest write failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
661			warnManifestNotWritten(out, "write to disk failed: "+err.Error())
662			return
663		}
664		writeReviewCompletionFooter(out, manifest)
665	}
666	
667	// warnManifestNotWritten prints a user-visible note explaining that the
668	// review skills ran but findings were not persisted, so `entire review
669	// --findings` and `entire review --fix` will not see this run. The reason
670	// string is appended verbatim and should describe the underlying cause in
671	// terms the user can act on (or at least diagnose with debug logs).
672	func warnManifestNotWritten(out io.Writer, reason string) {
673		fmt.Fprintln(out)
674		fmt.Fprintln(out, "Note: review skills ran but findings were not persisted.")
675		fmt.Fprintf(out, "  Reason: %s\n", reason)
676		fmt.Fprintln(out, "  `entire review --findings` and `entire review --fix` will not see this run.")
677		fmt.Fprintln(out, "  Re-run with `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` for diagnostic detail.")
678	}
679	
680	func composeSingleAgentSinks(in singleAgentSinkInputs) []reviewtypes.Sink {
681		if !in.isTTY || !in.canPrompt {
682			fmt.Fprintf(in.out, "Running review with %s...\n", in.agentName)
683			return []reviewtypes.Sink{DumpSink{W: in.out}}
684		}
685		return []reviewtypes.Sink{
686			NewTUISink([]string{in.agentName}, in.cancelRun, in.out),
687			DumpSink{W: in.out},
688		}
689	}
690	
691	func runConfigWithReviewConfig(base reviewtypes.RunConfig, cfg settings.ReviewConfig) reviewtypes.RunConfig {
692		applyReviewConfig(&base, cfg)
693		return base
694	}
695	
696	func applyReviewConfig(runCfg *reviewtypes.RunConfig, cfg settings.ReviewConfig) {
697		runCfg.Skills = cfg.Skills
698		if len(cfg.Skills) == 0 {
699			runCfg.PromptOverride = cfg.Prompt
700			return
701		}
702		runCfg.AlwaysPrompt = cfg.Prompt
703	}
704	
705	// findTUISink returns the first *TUISink in the slice (if any). Used by the
706	// caller to wire Start/Wait around the run without re-running composition.
707	func findTUISink(sinks []reviewtypes.Sink) (*TUISink, bool) {
708		for _, s := range sinks {
709			if t, ok := s.(*TUISink); ok {
710				return t, true
711			}
712		}
713		return nil, false
714	}
715	
716	// perAgentConfiguredReviewer is an AgentReviewer adapter that overrides the
717	// RunConfig passed to the underlying reviewer's Start method. This lets
718	// RunMulti pass a single shared RunConfig at the API boundary while each
719	// agent in a multi-agent run still sees its own skills and always-prompt.
720	type perAgentConfiguredReviewer struct {
721		inner reviewtypes.AgentReviewer
722		cfg   reviewtypes.RunConfig
723	}
724	
725	func (r *perAgentConfiguredReviewer) Name() string { return r.inner.Name() }
726	func (r *perAgentConfiguredReviewer) Start(ctx context.Context, _ reviewtypes.RunConfig) (reviewtypes.Process, error) {
727		return r.inner.Start(ctx, r.cfg) //nolint:wrapcheck // transparent adapter; callers see inner's error type directly
728	}
729	
730	// Compile-time interface check.
731	var _ reviewtypes.AgentReviewer = (*perAgentConfiguredReviewer)(nil)
732	
733	// currentHeadSHA returns the current HEAD commit hash as a 40-char hex string.
734	func currentHeadSHA(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) (string, error) {
735		out, err := runGit(ctx, repoRoot, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
736		if err != nil {
737			return "", fmt.Errorf("git rev-parse HEAD: %w", err)
738		}
739		return strings.TrimSpace(out), nil
740	}

26		SessionStateDirName = "entire-sessions"

28		// StaleSessionThreshold is the duration after which an ended session is considered stale
29		// and will be automatically deleted during load/list operations.
30		StaleSessionThreshold = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
31	
32		// StuckActiveThreshold is the duration after which an ACTIVE session with no
33		// interaction is considered stuck (used by "entire doctor" and "entire status").

37	// Kind identifies the purpose of a session. Empty means "normal" (legacy
38	// sessions + every session that isn't a review). Callers must not rely on
39	// Kind being set unless they specifically want to branch on it.
40	//
41	// Kind is a discriminator — it distinguishes review variants at a per-session
42	// granularity. The checkpoint-level HasReview flag remains an umbrella that
43	// any review-kind session should set (so future review kinds like manual
44	// review can be added without changing summary-shape).
45	type Kind string
46	
47	const (
48		// KindAgentReview tags a session created by `entire review` (agent-driven
49		// review). Future review kinds (e.g., manual review) should be defined as
50		// distinct Kind values AND added to Kind.IsReview so the checkpoint's
51		// HasReview umbrella flag keeps covering them.
52		KindAgentReview Kind = "agent_review"
53	)
54	
55	// IsReview reports whether this Kind counts as "a review happened" for the
56	// purpose of CheckpointSummary.HasReview. Extend this when adding new
57	// review-kind Kind values (e.g. KindManualReview) so the umbrella flag stays
58	// accurate without string-literal coupling across packages.
59	func (k Kind) IsReview() bool {
60		// Note: a switch is the natural shape here, but golangci's
61		// singleCaseSwitch flags a one-case switch — so we keep it as a list of
62		// equality checks. Add new review-kind values to the disjunction below.
63		return k == KindAgentReview
64	}
